subject.title: [Feature]: snapshot-cursor paging for oversized imported CLI transcripts in chat.history

question: Should imported CLI transcript paging extend current offsets through a shared implicit snapshot, or should the explicit cursor design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/87111 become the canonical `chat.history` contract?
rationale: Both approaches add lifecycle-sensitive core behavior, but they differ in public protocol surface, stale-page semantics, client migration, and shared gateway/TUI ownership; code inspection cannot determine the intended permanent contract.

options.title: Shared implicit snapshot
options.body: Materialize one bounded snapshot per session generation in the shared history layer and page it through the existing offset request shape.

options.title: Canonical explicit cursor
options.body: Adopt and broaden the older PR’s cursor protocol to cover imported snapshot lifetime, expiry, invalidation, and all relevant consumers.

options.title: Defer imported paging
options.body: Retain terminal-snapshot truncation honesty until gateway and TUI history are unified behind a broader service.

recommendation.title: Shared implicit snapshot
recommendation.body: Materialize one bounded snapshot per session generation in the shared history layer and page it through the existing offset request shape.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available protocol and feature-history evidence points to this person, who also authored the protected design issue.
